findings.evidence: The citation labels Teschl §9.6 as covering transfer matrices and transmission for piecewise-constant potentials. That section is “Spectral transformations II” and does not support the stated locator.
Binney & Skinner Chapter 4, pp. 65–88, is cited for rectangular-barrier transmission. The barrier treatment is in Chapter 5, §5.3, printed pp. 84–89.

The citation assigns finite-well root conditions and oscillation counting to Teschl §9.6, which is “Spectral transformations II.” The cited section does not support these claims; Theorem 9.40 is in §9.7 and has full-line hypotheses.
Binney & Skinner Chapter 4, pp. 65–88, is cited for finite square-well root conditions. The square-well treatment is in Chapter 5, §5.1, printed pp. 75–79.

The citation identifies Teschl §9.1 as the source of the simple Dirichlet nodal count. Theorem 9.40 is in §9.7 and concerns full-line eigenfunctions below essential spectrum, not the bounded-interval Dirichlet count.
Teschl Lemma 9.4 is cited as a Green-kernel/resolvent formula, but it concerns closure and adjoint domains of the minimal Sturm–Liouville operator. The Green-resolvent formula is Lemma 9.7 in §9.2.
The citation places separated self-adjoint boundary conditions and simplicity in Teschl §9.1. Theorem 9.6 on separated self-adjoint boundary conditions is in §9.2.
Teschl §3.2, pp. 89–92, is cited for Fourier/sine-basis completeness, but §3.2 is “More on Borel measures” and starts at printed p. 99. The cited locator does not support that claim.

Teschl §9.2 is cited for negative eigenvalues of point-interaction realizations, but that section concerns Sturm–Liouville endpoint classification, separated boundary conditions and Green kernels; it does not state the delta-interaction bound-state formula.
